hypotheses.reasoning: Before 02:28 the cache was healthy (#108 hits=14814) and logins took about 100ms. At 02:28:13 session-cache was restarted after a node replacement with no RDB snapshot and came back empty (#115). Its miss ratio then jumped to 95% (baseline 2%) and account-svc fell back to accounts-db for every request (#123). This flood of reads saturated accounts-db: connections reached 484-493 of 500 and CPU 95-98% (#124, #133). Simple primary-key lookups slowed to 7-8s (#139, #161), account-svc queries hit their 5s timeout (#138, #181), and edge-proxy returned 504s (#142, #159, #163, #184). The failure started at the cache and spread to the database, then to the gateway.
The direct cause of the timeouts is accounts-db running out of connections and CPU. However, that overload was triggered by the empty cache, so it is a step in the chain rather than the origin.
The timeouts to the dependency are what users see, not what started the incident.

verdict.recommendedAction: Short term: cap the load on accounts-db while the cache refills. Rate-limit or coalesce cache-miss loads in account-svc (single-flight / request collapsing), add a cap on concurrent DB loads, and consider briefly shedding /login traffic. Warm session-cache with hot account keys. Long term: turn on RDB/AOF persistence or replicas for session-cache so a replaced node doesn't come back empty, warm the cache before putting a replacement node into service, and add stampede protection (jittered TTLs, request coalescing).
